children: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NSE:SUNPHARMA) posted strong Q1 earnings and double‑digit India sales growth while securing an $12B bridge loan, high ratings and rights to lerodalcibep, positioning it for expansion as regulatory shifts may squeeze smaller rivals and a Rs15,000 crore NCD move looms.
: Sun Pharmaceutical reportedly secured an $12B 18-month bridge loan in early 2026 to fund its Organon acquisition; part was rupee debt and State Bank of India was a lender.
: Sun Pharmaceutical to meet Oct 12, 2026 to consider private placement of listed, rated, unsecured, redeemable non-convertible debentures up to Rs 15,000 crore.
Sun Pharma Q1 Net Profit Rise
: Sun Pharmaceutical (SUNPHARMA) Q1: net profit Rs 2,894.79 crore, up 27% YoY; revenue Rs 15,299.88 crore vs Rs 13,851.4 crore year‑ago.
: Sun Pharma reported September sales up 21.5% year‑on‑year in the Indian market, contributing to the IPM’s strongest monthly showing in three years.
: CARE reaffirmed AAA; Stable ratings for Sun Pharma’s Rs 10,000 crore infra bonds and Rs 2,000/500 crore Tier II bonds, assigned A1+ to its certificate of deposit; Tier II rating withdrawn.

: SUNPHARMA secured exclusive global rights (ex‑US/China) to manufacture, commercialize and license lerodalcibep, a PCSK9 inhibitor for lowering LDL‑C; deal includes upfront, milestones and royalties.
: Sun Pharma reported two-year LEQSELVI data: ~94% of Week-52 responders kept hair regrowth through Week-108; safety over two years remained consistent with prior experience.
UCPMP Rules May Benefit Sun Pharma
: Sun Pharmaceutical (SUNPHARMA) could benefit if stricter UCPMP enforcement forces smaller rivals out; outcomes hinge on upcoming panel recommendations and regulator actions affecting compliance.
